title: A Serverless Edge-Native Data Processing Architecture for Autonomous Driving Training
evidence: Supporting infrastructure, not a demonstrated driving policy.

title: AROLA: A Modular Layered Architecture for Scaled Autonomous Racing
device: NVIDIA Jetson; exact variant not specified in reviewed hardware passage
evidence: Section III-C identifies Jetson. Paper reports RoboRacer IV25 deployment. Linked code is the minimal example cited in the paper, not a claim that the entire architecture and Race Monitor are released. Hardware variant remains unknown.

title: EdgeVTP: Exploration of Latency-efficient Trajectory Prediction for Edge-based Embedded Vision Applications
method: Bounded interaction graph; lightweight temporal model; one-shot curve decoding
evidence: CVF paper and author repository agree on edge evaluation. Highway surveillance prediction is an adjacent supporting task, not ego-vehicle steering or physical autonomous driving. Repository H100 timing table must not be read as Jetson timing.

title: Efficient Real-World Autonomous Racing via Attenuated Residual Policy Optimization
evidence: Manuscript identifies onboard compute and author code. Training progressively removes the base controller, leaving a standalone deployed neural policy. Reported latency includes preprocessing and ROS 2 publishing; not compared as a universal benchmark.

title: NeoRacer: An Open, Standardized 1:12 Scale Autonomous Race Car for Benchmarking and Education
device: Jetson Orin Nano; LiDAR, global-shutter camera and IMU
evidence: Author manuscript links an organization containing the resources, not one paper-specific repository. No peer-reviewed venue asserted. Platform demonstrations are not a comprehensive control-algorithm benchmark.

title: Pocket Racer: An accessible autonomous racing educational platform
method: Behavior cloning; CNN, 3D CNN, LRCN and ViT benchmarks
evidence: Published 29 April 2026. Publisher hardware and data-availability sections identify the board and code. Dataset is available upon request, not assumed freely downloadable. Quartile not independently verified.

title: A Comparative Study of Scaled Autonomous Vehicle Platforms for Research and Education
device: Quanser QCar; MIT RACECAR; SunFounder PiCar
task: Platform selection for research and education
evidence: IEEE abstract and proceedings metadata verified. This is a platform comparison, not a new end-to-end driving model or an independent experiment for every reviewed platform. MHTC is not treated as ICRA/IROS-equivalent by association with IEEE.

title: Efficient On-Chip Implementation of 4D Radar-Based 3D Object Detection on Hailo-8L
method: Reshaped radar neural-network operations for accelerator compatibility
evidence: Do not equate accelerator throughput with end-to-end vehicle control frequency.

title: Enhancing Safety in Autonomous Racing With Constrained Reinforcement Learning
device: Real 1:10 racecar; exact onboard processor not verified
evidence: Publisher abstract confirms zero-shot physical deployment. Included as a scaled-car study; no Pi/Jetson model or resource-efficiency claim is inferred.

title: Learning-Based On-Track System Identification for Scaled Autonomous Racing in Under a Minute
device: Scaled ForzaETH vehicle; exact compute not independently verified
evidence: 2024 preprint, 2025 journal article. Shared ecosystem code; do not assume every branch reproduces this paper.

title: ResAwareWoR
device: Target hardware must be checked per experiment
evidence: Publication venue not established; kept as project rather than peer-reviewed evidence.

title: Route-centric ant-inspired memories enable panoramic route-following in a car-like robot
device: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B; panoramic camera
method: Insect mushroom-body-inspired visual memory; self-supervised route learning
evidence: Published 24 September 2025. Methods identify Antcar onboard Pi 4; code availability links Zenodo. Low computational power figures must not be interpreted as whole-vehicle electrical power. Quartile not independently verified.

title: Tackling Snow-Induced Challenges: Safe Autonomous Lane-Keeping with Robust Reinforcement Learning
evidence: Section V identifies onboard hardware and real-platform fine-tuning. Snow scenarios are principally simulation evidence; do not infer a certified winter-road system or zero-shot transfer. No author code repository was identified.

title: TimelyNet: Adaptive Neural Architecture for Autonomous Driving with Dynamic Deadline
evidence: Author PDF: https://tanrui.github.io/pub/TimelyNet-EMSOFT.pdf ; hardware evaluation is not evidence of physical road driving. Official archived artifact preferred over an unconfirmed GitHub match.

title: Towards Accurate and Efficient 3D Object Detection for Autonomous Driving: A Mixture of Experts Computing System on Edge
method: EMC2 multimodal mixture of experts; routing and graph/memory optimization
evidence: CVF PDF experiment section specifies AGX Orin and first-page footnote supplies code. IEEE indexing date is 2026, but conference year is 2025. Do not repeat the manuscript wording about a greater-than-100% latency reduction; reported speedups are not equivalent to such reductions. Potentially related EMOS TPAMI paper is held out pending overlap review.

title: VLDrive: Vision-Augmented Lightweight MLLMs for Efficient Language-grounded Autonomous Driving
method: 1.3B-parameter MLLM; visual-token pruning and memory aggregation
evidence: Included only as an efficiency-oriented algorithmic comparison. CVF abstract links author code and reports simulator evaluation. Lightweight relative to a 7B model does not imply feasibility on Pi or a small Jetson.

title: A platform-agnostic deep reinforcement learning framework for effective Sim2Real transfer towards autonomous driving
evidence: Paper and author page identify two Duckiebot hardware versions. Journal quartile not verified.

title: Autonomous Driving Small-Scale Cars: A Survey of Recent Development
device: Pi, Jetson and other scaled-car platforms
evidence: Authors: Dianzhao Li, Paul Auerbach and Ostap Okhrin. Used for discovery; individual primary sources determine catalog claims.

title: Development and Control of an Autonomous RC Racing Car
device: Jetson Nano onboard; longitudinal speed command from host
method: Identified vehicle model; PID, MPC and LQR comparison
task: Lateral control on a marked track
evidence: Publisher assigns volume year 2024 (MECC 2024), although DOI includes 2025. Onboard lateral control is not fully independent autonomy because the velocity command comes from a host over ROS.

title: ForzaETH Race Stack—Scaled Autonomous Head-to-Head Racing on Fully Commercial Off-the-Shelf Hardware
device: Intel Core i7-8850U; onboard x86, no GPU
evidence: Adjacent small-vehicle x86 platform, not a Pi/Jetson experiment. Primary project: https://www.forzaeth.ch/blog/full_system_paper/

title: HARD: Hardware-Aware Lightweight Real-Time Semantic Segmentation Model Deployable from Edge to GPU
method: Hardware-scaled segmentation variants; dual atrous pooling
evidence: CVF PDF sections 4.1 and 4.4 specify embedded boards. MCU variant and resolution differ from GPU variants; do not combine accuracy from one setting with FPS from another. No closed-loop vehicle demonstrated.

title: Model Optimization in Deep Learning Based Robot Control for Autonomous Driving
device: Constrained-compute evaluation; exact board not verified
evidence: 2023 online-first / 2024 issue and ICRA presentation are one work. No physical edge-car claim. Evaluation tool: https://github.com/JdeRobot/BehaviorMetrics

title: Nigel—Mechatronic Design and Robust Sim2Real Control of an Overactuated Autonomous Vehicle
evidence: Final journal version 2024; AutoDRIVE is the ecosystem hub, not a standalone paper reproduction package.

title: Real-Time 3D Object Detection Using InnovizOne LiDAR and Low-Power Hailo-8 AI Accelerator
evidence: Preprint status; no physical closed-loop driving evidence. Canonical GitHub URL checked separately because paper text contains spacing artifacts.

title: The Effects of Speed and Delays on Test-Time Performance of End-to-End Self-Driving
evidence: DOI 10.3390/s24061963. Earlier arXiv 2312.06670 is the same work with a different title; supplementary data: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.24948690

title: TinyLidarNet: 2D LiDAR-based End-to-End Deep Learning Model for F1TENTH Autonomous Racing
device: Jetson NX; ESP32-S3 and Raspberry Pi Pico inference ports
method: 1D CNN; behavior cloning; INT8 TFLite Micro
validation: Real + simulation; additional MCU inference benchmarks
evidence: Author repository confirms IROS 2024 despite later indexing dates. Physical racing is distinguished from MCU inference timing. Author manuscript: https://ittc.ku.edu/~heechul/papers/tiny-iros2024-camera.pdf

title: Unifying F1TENTH Autonomous Racing: Survey, Methods and Benchmarks
evidence: No uniform onboard deployment claim for all included algorithms.

title: A Survey on Approximate Edge AI for Energy Efficient Autonomous Driving Services
evidence: Survey context, not a new hardware experiment.

title: AutoDRIVE: A Comprehensive, Flexible and Integrated Digital Twin Ecosystem for Autonomous Driving Research & Education
method: Digital twins, perception and control tooling
evidence: DOI 10.3390/robotics12030077. Nigel/AutoDRIVE papers share infrastructure but address distinct contributions; do not count them as independent hardware platforms.

title: Bypassing the Simulation-to-Reality Gap: Online Reinforcement Learning Using a Supervisor
device: Jetson NX as described in manuscript; 1:10 F1TENTH
task: Online learning on physical racing car
evidence: arXiv v2 hardware description identifies the board; author proceedings PDF confirms ICAR 2023: https://f1tenth.github.io/publications/Simulation-to-Reality_Gap.pdf . Preprint 2022 and Xplore indexing 2024 do not change proceedings year. Onboard control does not establish that every training step is computed onboard.

title: Chronos and CRS: Design of a Miniature Car-Like Robot and a Software Framework for Single and Multi-Agent Robotics and Control
device: ESP32-WROOM32D onboard; CRS communicates over Wi-Fi
method: Low-level MCU control; MPC and safety-filter framework
evidence: 2022 preprint / 2023 proceedings. ESP32 executes low-level loops; do not describe the complete MPC pipeline as onboard TinyML.

title: ES3Net: Accurate and Efficient Edge-Based Self-Supervised Stereo Matching Network
validation: Depth dataset and edge inference evaluation
evidence: CVF abstract identifies TX2 and repository confirms authorship. Relevant as a perception component; the paper also targets drones and is not a closed-loop road-driving demonstration. Workshop status is explicit.

title: High-Speed Autonomous Racing Using Trajectory-Aided Deep Reinforcement Learning
evidence: Useful control baseline; excluded from physical embedded-deployment evidence.

title: Neural Network Models for Driving Control of Indoor Autonomous Vehicles in Mobile Edge Computing
device: Raspberry Pi + LiDAR; exact board not verified
evidence: DOI 10.3390/s23052575; open full text: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10007646/

title: Run Your 3D Object Detector on NVIDIA Jetson Platforms: A Benchmark Analysis
device: Jetson Nano, TX2, Xavier NX and AGX-family boards
evidence: DOI 10.3390/s23084005. Does not establish closed-loop autonomous driving.

title: Towards Safety Assured End-to-End Vision-Based Control for Autonomous Racing
device: Jetson TX2, 8GB; twin ZED camera; 1:10 RC car
method: Imitation learning and state prediction with control barrier functions
evidence: Manuscript section 5.2 identifies TX2 onboard. Venue confirmed by author lab: https://air.egr.uh.edu/research/high-performance-control-of-agile-robots/ . Do not label it ICRA solely because adjacent author publications appeared there.

title: VAD: Vectorized Scene Representation for Efficient Autonomous Driving
method: Vectorized scene representation; VAD-Base and VAD-Tiny
evidence: CVF record confirms title, venue and code. Efficiency baseline only: open-loop planning metrics and relative speedup are not evidence of physical embedded closed-loop driving.

title: Autonomous Vehicles on the Edge: A Survey on Autonomous Vehicle Racing
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems
evidence: “On the edge” includes limits of racing performance; title alone does not establish resource-constrained computing.

title: DeepPicar-v3
evidence: Offboard/Colab training; repository creation year is not a paper publication year.

title: DeepPicarMicro: Applying TinyML to Autonomous Cyber Physical Systems
method: TFLite Micro; quantized and optimized PilotNet
evidence: MCU runs inference onboard; offboard training is distinct. Author camera-ready and repository verified.

title: Latent Imagination Facilitates Zero-Shot Transfer in Autonomous Racing
device: Jetson TX2; F1TENTH and Hokuyo LiDAR
method: Dreamer world models; latent-space policy learning
evidence: IEEE publication identity and arXiv v3 hardware setup confirm the venue and onboard TX2. Preprint 2021 / proceedings 2022, counted once. Authors include Axel Brunnbauer and Luigi Berducci; do not copy misattributed author lists from secondary platform indexes.

title: Learning to drive fast on a DuckieTown highway
task: Visual lane following at different speeds
evidence: Use 2022 proceedings year, not draft upload date. Author lab confirms April 2022: https://www.intelligentroboticslab.nl/robots/duckiebot/ ; manuscript: https://pure.uva.nl/ws/files/59613018/MCAS_paper_wiggers_v4.pdf

title: Miniature Autonomy as Means to Find New Approaches in Reliable Autonomous Driving AI Method Design
device: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 + Coral Edge TPU
method: Detection and path tracking; pure pursuit / TEB
evidence: Road-vehicle part included; aerial-robot examples outside scope. Coral acceleration does not imply all control runs on TPU.

title: An Efficient and Scalable Simulation Model for Autonomous Vehicles With Economical Hardware
device: Single Raspberry Pi; exact revision not verified
method: Lightweight deep learning; camera and ultrasonic sensing
task: Track following, traffic signs and obstacle avoidance
evidence: University publication record explicitly describes a physical car despite the title. Online-first 2020, issue March 2021; counted once. Primary institutional record: https://researchportal.tuni.fi/en/publications/an-efficient-and-scalable-simulation-model-for-autonomous-vehicle/

title: ProAI: An Efficient Embedded AI Hardware for Automotive Applications — A Benchmark Study
device: ZF ProAI and Jetson Nano; workstation baseline
evidence: Primary CVF paper: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/ICCV2021W/ERCVAD/papers/Mantowsky_ProAI_An_Efficient_Embedded_AI_Hardware_for_Automotive_Applications_-_ICCVW_2021_paper.pdf . ProAI is automotive compute, not a miniature car. Board-level inference/power comparison does not demonstrate complete autonomous control.

title: Vision-Based Autonomous Car Racing Using Deep Imitative Reinforcement Learning
evidence: Author project page; linked platform code must not be assumed to reproduce the full DIRL method.

title: F1TENTH: An Open-source Evaluation Environment for Continuous Control and Reinforcement Learning
evidence: Publication year 2020; competition track, not NeurIPS main track. Paper hardware section specifies TX2; gym link is simulator code.

title: Go-CHART: A Miniature Remotely Accessible Self-Driving Car Robot
device: Pi 3B, Pi Zero and Teensy; external Jetson TX2
evidence: Not a fully self-contained Pi-only autonomy demonstration. The similarly named wcharczuk/go-chart is unrelated plotting software.

title: DeepPiCar
method: OpenCV lane following and TensorFlow perception
evidence: Different project from DeepPicar; individual neural tasks can use Coral, not all control operations.

title: JetRacer
evidence: Legacy ecosystem reference; repository age/activity is not a support guarantee.

title: DeepPicar: A Low-cost Deep Neural Network-based Autonomous Car
evidence: Pre-2020 foundation; distinct from dctian/DeepPiCar.

title: DonkeyCar
evidence: Legacy platform used by 2020–2026 studies. Current device support depends on release; training may be offboard.
